subject: Computer Networking
title: Phishing Detection
description: Learn Phishing Detection in one minute.

hook.text: The email looks exactly like your bank. The link goes to a fake site. Phishing detection catches it.

buildup.text: Filters check URLs against known phishing databases. They also analyze visual similarity to real sites.

discovery.text: Machine learning models examine tone, urgency, and sender patterns. 'Your account will be locked' is a red flag.

twist.text: Spear phishing targets individuals with personal details. Generic filters miss these. Context is needed.

climax.text: Modern filters sandbox links — opening them in a virtual browser to check for credential harvesting pages.

punchline.text: Phishing detection layers rules, ML, and sandboxing. Defense in depth.

quiz.question: What does link sandboxing do in phishing detection?
options: Opens links in a virtual browser to check for threats
Blocks all links in every email

details.summary: Phishing emails impersonate trusted senders to trick recipients into revealing credentials or clicking malicious links. Detection combines URL analysis, sender authentication checks, content pattern matching, and machine learning to identify deceptive messages before they reach the inbox.
details.whyItMatters: Phishing is the primary vector for cyberattacks. Detecting and blocking phishing emails prevents credential theft, malware infections, and financial fraud.
takeaways: Phishing impersonates trusted senders to steal credentials
Detection uses URL analysis, authentication, and machine learning
Human awareness training remains essential alongside technology

faq.question: What makes phishing emails hard to detect technically?
faq.answer: Sophisticated phishing uses lookalike domains, compromised legitimate accounts, and personalized content that passes automated filters. Spear phishing targets specific individuals with context-appropriate messages. The best phishing emails are nearly indistinguishable from legitimate ones.

faq.question: How do modern email systems detect phishing?
faq.answer: They check URL destinations against known phishing databases, analyze sender authentication results, scan for impersonation patterns, and use machine learning trained on millions of examples. Some systems create safe previews of links to detect malicious destinations.
